questions.topic_text: Topic 1.11: Goodwill/capital reserve on acquisition, net of pre-acquisition dividend and asset/investment revaluation

topics.topic_name: Calculation of Goodwill/Capital Reserve (Cost of Control)

questions.why: Rank 8 topic (Calculation of Goodwill/Capital Reserve (Cost of Control)); Category A — 99% identical to an ICAI Study Material question; MTP September 2025 Set 1.
questions.question_html:
Exe Ltd. acquires 70% of equity shares of Zed Ltd. as on 31st March, 2024 at a cost of ₹70 lakhs. The following information is available from the balance sheet of Zed Ltd. as on 31st March, 2024 (₹ in lakhs): Property, plant and equipment 120; Investments 55; Current Assets 70; Loans & Advances 15; 15% Debentures 90; Current Liabilities 50. The following revaluations have been agreed upon (not included in the above figures): Property, plant and equipment up by 20%; Investments down by 10%.

Zed Ltd. declared and paid dividend @20% on its equity shares as on 31st March, 2024 (Face value – ₹10 per share). Exe Ltd. purchased the shares of Zed Ltd. @₹20 per share.

Calculate the amount of goodwill/capital reserve on acquisition of shares of Zed Ltd.
questions.answer_html:
Cost of Control:

ParticularsComputation₹
ACost of InvestmentsGiven70,00,000
Less: Dividend out of Pre-Acquisition Dividend3.5 Lacs × ₹10 (FV) × 20% (No. of Shares = 70 Lacs/20 = 3.5 Lacs)(7,00,000)
Subtotal A63,00,000
BShare in Net Assets of Zed Ltd.1,38,50,000 × 70%96,95,000
CGoodwill / (Capital Reserve)A − B33,95,000

Working notes:

1. Calculation of Net Assets:

Particulars₹
Property, Plant & Equipment (120+20%)1,44,00,000
Investment (55 − 10%)49,50,000
Current Assets70,00,000
Loans & Advances15,00,000
Subtotal A2,78,50,000
15% Debentures90,00,000
Current Liabilities50,00,000
Subtotal B1,40,00,000
Net Assets (A−B)1,38,50,000

2. No. of shares acquired = Cost of investment / Purchase price per share = 70,00,000 / ₹20 = 3,50,000 shares.
questions.mistake_text: Author’s Note: A common error here is treating the entire dividend received from the subsidiary as post-acquisition income, without first identifying and deducting the pre-acquisition portion from the cost of investment.

questions.topic_text: Topic 1.11: Cost of control - goodwill/capital reserve against revalued net assets, net of pre-acquisition dividend

topics.topic_name: Calculation of Goodwill/Capital Reserve (Cost of Control)

questions.why: Rank 8 topic (Calculation of Goodwill/Capital Reserve (Cost of Control)); Category A — 98% identical to an ICAI Study Material question; MTP January 2025 Set 2.
questions.question_html: Exe Ltd. acquires 70% of equity shares of Zed Ltd. as on 31st March, 2024 at a cost of ₹70 lakhs. The following information is available from the balance sheet of Zed Ltd. as on 31st March, 2024: Property, plant and equipment ₹120 lakhs, Investments ₹55 lakhs, Current Assets ₹70 lakhs, Loans & Advances ₹15 lakhs, 15% Debentures ₹90 lakhs, Current Liabilities ₹50 lakhs. The following revaluations have been agreed upon (not included in the above figures): Property, plant and equipment up by 20%, Investments down by 10%. Zed Ltd. declared and paid dividend @ 20% on its equity shares as on 31st March, 2024 (Face value – ₹10 per share). Exe Ltd. purchased the shares of Zed Ltd. @ ₹20 per share. Calculate the amount of goodwill/capital reserve on acquisition of shares of Zed Ltd.
questions.answer_html:
Revalued net assets of Zed Ltd. as on 31.03.2024:

Particulars₹ in lakhs
Property Plant & Equipment [120 × 120%]144.0
Investments [55 × 90%]49.5
Current Assets70.0
Loans & Advances15.0
Total Assets after revaluation278.5
Less: 15% Debentures (90.0) and Current Liabilities (50.0)(140.0)
Equity / Net Worth138.50
Exe Ltd.'s share of net assets (70% of 138.50)96.95
Exe Ltd.'s cost of acquisition of shares of Zed Ltd. (₹70 lakhs − ₹7 lakhs pre-acquisition dividend*)63.00
Capital Reserve33.95

*Total Cost of 70% Equity of Zed Ltd. ₹70 lakhs; Purchase Price of each share ₹20; Number of shares purchased (70 lakhs/20) 3.50 lakhs; Dividend @ 20% i.e. ₹2/share = ₹7 lakhs. Since dividend received is for the pre-acquisition period, it has been reduced from the cost of investment in the subsidiary company.
questions.mistake_text: Author’s Note: A common error is comparing the cost of investment against the subsidiary's unrevalued net assets, or failing to net the pre-acquisition dividend against the cost of investment before computing goodwill or capital reserve.

questions.topic_text: Topic 1.12: Minority interest computed at acquisition date and consolidation date across five independent cases
questions.why: Rank 18 topic (Minority Interests); 66% match to an ICAI Study Material question; MTP September 2025 Set 1.
questions.question_html:
From the following data, determine Minority Interest on the date of acquisition and on the date of consolidation in each case:

CaseSubsidiary Company% of Share OwnedCost (₹) Share Capital 01-01-2024 (₹)Profit and Loss A/c 01-01-2024 (₹) Share Capital 31-12-2024 (₹)Profit and Loss A/c 31-12-2024 (₹)
Case-iX85%1,85,0001,35,00060,0001,35,00070,000
Case-iiY70%1,60,0001,25,00045,0001,25,0005,000
Case-iiiZ65%83,00025,0005,00025,0005,000
Case-ivM90%60,00045,00020,00045,00040,000
Case-vN100%85,00025,00025,00025,00050,000
questions.answer_html:
Minority Interest = Equity attributable to minorities. Equity is the residual interest in the assets of an enterprise after deducting all its liabilities, i.e. in this case, it should equal Share Capital + Profit & Loss A/c. Let A = Share capital on 1.1.2024, B = Profit & loss account balance on 1.1.2024, C = Share capital on 31.12.2024, D = Profit & loss account balance on 31.12.2024.

CaseMinority % [E]Minority interest as at date of acquisition [E]×[A+B] (₹) Minority interest as at date of consolidation [E]×[C+D] (₹)
Case-i [100-85]15%29,25030,750
Case-ii [100-70]30%51,00039,000
Case-iii [100-65]35%10,50010,500
Case-iv [100-90]10%6,5008,500
Case-v [100-100]NILNILNIL
questions.mistake_text: Author’s Note: A common error here is computing minority interest only from the closing share capital and reserves figures, without separately building up the acquisition-date minority interest as its own reference point.

(iii) Glamour Ltd. purchased goods worth ₹5,00,000 (Invoice Price) from Fashion Ltd. at a profit of 25% on cost; 50% still in stock of Glamour Ltd. questions.topic_text: Topic 1.14: Revaluation of a subsidiary's asset on acquisition, split between capital (pre-acquisition) profit and post-acquisition additional depreciation
questions.why: Rank 9 topic (Consolidation Adjustments); 53% match to an ICAI Study Material question; MTP May 2024 Set 2.
questions.question_html: Gamma Ltd. acquired 24,000 equity shares of ₹10 each, in Beta Ltd. on October 1, 2023 for ₹4,60,200. The profit and loss account of Beta Ltd. showed a balance of ₹15,000 on April 1, 2023. The plant and machinery of Beta Ltd. which stood in the books at ₹2,25,000 on April 1, 2023 was considered worth ₹2,70,000 on the date of acquisition. The information of the two companies as at 31-3-2024 was as follows: Share capital (fully paid equity shares of ₹10 each): Gamma 7,50,000, Beta 3,00,000. General reserve: Gamma 3,60,000, Beta 1,50,000. Profit and loss account: Gamma 85,800, Beta 1,23,000. Current Liabilities: Gamma 2,54,700, Beta 49,500. Land and building: Gamma 2,70,000, Beta 2,85,000. Plant and machinery: Gamma 3,60,000, Beta 2,02,500. Investments: Gamma 4,60,200. Current assets: Gamma 3,60,300, Beta 1,35,000. You are required to compute impact of revaluation of Plant and Machinery.
questions.answer_html:
Impact of Revaluation of Plant and Machinery:

ParticularsAmount (₹)
Book value of Plant and Machinery as on 01-04-20232,25,000
Depreciation Rate [(2,25,000−2,02,500)/2,25,000 = 22,500/2,25,000×100]10%
Book value of P&M as on 01-10-2023 after 6 months' depreciation @10% (2,25,000−11,250)2,13,750
Revalued at2,70,000
Revaluation profit (2,70,000−2,13,750)56,250
Share of Gamma Ltd. in Revaluation Profit (80%)45,000
Share of Minority in Revaluation profit (20%)11,250
Additional Depreciation on appreciated value to be charged from post-acquisition profits [(10% of 2,25,000 for 6 months) + (10% of 2,70,000 for 6 months) less 22,500 already charged]2,250
Share of Gamma Ltd. in additional depreciation, reducing its 80% share of post-acquisition profit by1,800
Share of Minority Interest in additional depreciation450

Working note — percentage of holding: Holding Co.: 24,000 shares (80%); Minority shareholders: 6,000 shares (20%); Total shares: 30,000 (i.e. Beta Ltd.'s ₹3,00,000 share capital ÷ ₹10 face value).
questions.mistake_text: Author’s Note: A common error here is computing the additional depreciation on the revalued asset for the full year rather than only the post-acquisition 6-month period (1 October 2023 to 31 March 2024), or forgetting to net off the depreciation already charged on the original book value before arriving at the incremental amount.

6. Calculation of Revaluation Profit/Loss: Balance as on 01.04.2023 (given) 2,50,000; Depreciation for 6 months (2,50,000 × 10% × 6/12) (12,500); WDV as on date of acquisition 2,37,500; Revalued amount 2,20,000; Revaluation Loss 17,500.

7. Savings in Depreciation = Depreciation Provided for 6 months − Depreciation Should be = 12,500 − (2,20,000 × 10% × 6/12) = 1,500.

8. Calculation of provision reversed: Trade Receivable (Given) = 1,68,300 is after provision i.e. 99%. So, 100% will be 1,70,000; therefore provision will be 1,700.

As per para 20 and 21 of AS 21, Consolidated financial statements should be prepared using uniform accounting policies for like transactions and other events in similar circumstances. If it is not practicable to use uniform accounting policies in preparing the consolidated financial statements, that fact should be disclosed together with the proportions of the items in the consolidated financial statements to which the different accounting policies have been applied.

Some examinees misclassified main and sub-heads. Many did not correctly account for revaluation loss and depreciation savings, leading to incorrect analysis of profit and its allocation between the holding company and minority interest. Additionally, some examinees did not compute minority interest and capital reserve (cost of control) correctly.

questions.topic_text: Topic 1.6: Consolidation with a mid-year bonus issue from pre-acquisition reserves and unrealised profit on an upstream (subsidiary-to-parent) inter-company sale
questions.question_html: Seva Limited and subsidiary Meva Limited, Balance Sheets as at 31st March 2025 (₹ Lakh): Seva — Equity Shares of ₹10 6,000, General Reserve 1,500, P&L 2,000, 10% Debentures 1,180, Trade Payable 1,500; Land and Building 4,000, Plant & Machinery 1,460, Investments (Meva shares) 3,000, Inventories 1,400, Trade Receivable 1,420, Cash at Bank 550, Cash in Hand 350. Meva — Equity Shares of ₹10 4,000, General Reserve 1,200, P&L 1,500, 10% Debentures 820, Trade Payable 1,080; Land and Building 4,150, Plant & Machinery 1,650, Inventories 1,100, Trade Receivable 1,000, Cash at Bank 600, Cash in Hand 100. Seva acquired 80% of Meva on 1st April 2024 (Meva's General Reserve ₹2,000 lakh, P&L ₹800 lakh on that date). On 1st November 2024, Meva issued a 1:3 bonus share out of General Reserve (as at 31 March 2024 balance). On 31st March 2025, Seva's inventory includes goods purchased from Meva for ₹125 lakh, on which Meva made a profit of ₹25 lakh. Prepare the Consolidated Balance Sheet as per Schedule III.
questions.answer_html:
W.N.9 Bonus shares: Meva's shares post-bonus 4,000 lakh (at ₹10 face value, i.e. 400 lakh shares) represent 4/3 of pre-bonus holding; pre-bonus = 4,000×3/4=3,000; bonus issued = 4,000−3,000=1,000 (lakh, i.e. ₹1,000 lakh face value), funded from General Reserve.

W.N.1 Meva's General Reserve movement: Opening 2,000 − Bonus 1,000 + transfer from P&L 200 = Closing 1,200.

W.N.2 Meva's P&L movement: Opening 800 − transfer to General Reserve 200 + Net profit for the year (balancing) 900 = Closing 1,500.

W.N.4 Capital profits (pre-acquisition): General Reserve at acquisition, net of the bonus issue (2,000−1,000=1,000) + P&L at acquisition (800) = 1,800. Seva's 80% share = 1,440; Minority's 20% = 360.

W.N.3 Revenue profits (post-acquisition): 900 (from W.N.2); Seva's 80% share: General Reserve 160 (80% of 200) + P&L 560 (80% of 700, i.e. profit after removing the amount already transferred to reserve) = 720; Minority's 20% = 180.

W.N.5 Capital Reserve: Paid-up value of shares held (80% of 4,000) 3,200 + share in capital profits 1,440 = 4,640; less cost of shares 3,000 = Capital Reserve ₹1,640 lakh.

W.N.6 Minority Interest: 20% of share capital (800) + share in revenue profits (180) + share in capital profits (360) = 1,340; less unrealised profit (20% of 25 = 5, Meva's share of the inter-company profit since Meva is the seller) = Minority Interest ₹1,335 lakh.

Consolidated Balance Sheet as at 31st March, 2025 (₹ Lakh): Share Capital 6,000 (Seva's own, unchanged); Reserves and Surplus 5,840 (Capital Reserve 1,640 + General Reserve 1,660 + P&L 2,540); Minority Interest 1,335; Long-term borrowings 2,000 (1,180+820); Trade payables 2,580 (1,500+1,080). Total 17,755. Assets: PPE 11,260 (Land&Building 8,150 [4,000+4,150] + Plant&Machinery 3,110 [1,460+1,650]); Inventories 2,475 (1,400+1,100−25 unrealised profit); Trade receivables 2,420 (1,420+1,000); Cash and cash equivalents 1,600 (Bank 1,150 + Cash in hand 450). Total 17,755.
questions.mistake_text: Examiner’s Comment: Many examinees were unable to prepare the Balance Sheet and Notes to Accounts as per Schedule III. Several examinees failed to give the correct treatment to the issue of bonus shares and the unrealised profit included in closing inventory arising from an upstream transaction. Due to these errors, the computation of capital profits (pre-acquisition) and revenue profits (post-acquisition) was incorrect, which further affected the final answers.

To bring MNT Ltd.'s inventories values in line with those of LTC Ltd., its value of inventory is required to be reduced by ₹5,000 at the end of 2022-2023 and increased by ₹12,000 at the end of 2023-2024. (4) Prepaid expenses in MNT Ltd. include Sales Promotion expenditure carried forward of ₹25,000 in 2022-23 and ₹12,500 in 2023-24 being part of initial Sales Promotion expenditure of ₹37,500 in 2022-23, which is being written off over three years. Similar nature of Sales Promotion expenditure of LTC Ltd. has been fully written off in 2022-23.

Restate the balance sheet of MNT Ltd. as on 31st March, 2024 after considering the above information for the purpose of consolidation. Such restatement is necessary to make the accounting policies adopted by LTC Ltd. and MNT Ltd. uniform.

questions.mistake_text: Author’s Note: A recurring error is adjusting only the inventory-valuation difference for uniform accounting policies while forgetting that the doubtful-debts provision rate and the deferred sales-promotion write-off period also need to be restated to the parent's policy before consolidation.
